prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — to pick the right lawyer it helps to know more about your case. A few quick questions first:

- When did the accident happen?
- Were you injured (briefly describe injuries/severity)?
- Was the other driver insured? Were you at fault or unsure?
- Any police report, photos, medical records already?
- Do you want to sue the other driver, deal with your insurer, or both?
- Do you prefer a local Pleasanton/Alameda County attorney, or a larger firm that handles serious/catastrophic injury cases statewide?

If you’d rather I outline how to choose and find attorneys, here’s a practical guide you can use right away.

How to choose the right personal-injury lawyer
- Focus on auto-accident/personal-injury experience: Look for lawyers who regularly handle automobile collisions and bodily-injury claims in California.
- Local knowledge: An attorney familiar with Pleasanton/Alameda County courts, local insurers, and medical providers is a plus.
- Trial experience and resources: If your case might need to go to trial (or involves catastrophic injury), pick a lawyer or firm with courtroom experience and the financial resources to investigate and litigate.
- Contingency-fee agreement: Most PI lawyers work on contingency (they’re paid a percentage of the recovery). Confirm the percentage and how costs (expert fees, filing fees) are handled.
- Track record and client reviews: Look for settlements/verdicts in cases similar to yours and consistent positive client feedback.
- Communication and availability: Ask how often they’ll update you and who you’ll deal with day-to-day (attorney vs. paralegal).
- Fee fairness and transparency: Make sure you understand costs if the case settles vs. goes to trial.

Where to find attorneys
- Alameda County Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service
- California State Bar website (to check attorney license and discipline history)
- Consumer-review sites: Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Google/Yelp (read multiple reviews)
- Personal recommendations (friends, family, medical providers)

Important deadlines and practical notes
- Statute of limitations: In California you generally have 2 years from the date of injury to file a personal-injury lawsuit (there are exceptions — e.g., claims against government entities have much shorter notice periods). Don’t delay contacting a lawyer.
- Preserve evidence: Keep photos, medical records, police report, witness info, repair estimates, and any communication with insurers.
- Don’t give recorded statements to insurers without counsel; notify your insurer per your policy but speak to a lawyer before detailed recorded statements.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many auto-injury cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Have you handled cases like mine (injury type/severity)? Can you share results?
- How do you charge (contingency %)? What costs would I be responsible for if there is no recovery?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- What is your anticipated timeline and strategy?
- How will you communicate case developments?

Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific recovery amount
- Pressure to sign immediately without reviewing the retainer
- Unclear fee structure or refusal to put fee terms in writing
- Poor responsiveness during initial contact

If you want, I can:
- Look up lawyers in Pleasanton/Alameda County and give a short list of well-reviewed personal-injury attorneys (tell me if you want local solo attorneys or larger firms).
- Help draft an email or script to use when calling firms.
- Review names of attorneys you find and help compare them.

Tell me which of the follow-up options you prefer and give any case details you’re comfortable sharing.
